question:
Calculate P15 for the data given below:

6, 24, 36, 12, 20, 10
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Arrange in ascending order: 6, 10, 12, 20, 24, 36 ⇒ n = 6

P15 = value at position (15/100) × (n + 1) = 0.15 × 7 = 1.05th position

P15 = L + 0.05 × (next value − current value)

= 6 + 0.05 × (10 − 6) = 6 + 0.05 × 4 = 6 + 0.2 = 6.2

**∴ The correct answer is P15 = 6.2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Data: 6, 24, 36, 12, 20, 10

n = 6 observations

Find P15 (15th Percentile)

**Formula used:**

Step 1: Arrange data in ascending order.

Step 2: Position of Pp = p/100 × (n + 1)

Step 3: If position is not a whole number, interpolate between two values.

Interpolation: Pp = lower value + decimal part × (upper value − lower value)

 Sorted
